result.title: AstroPIE-53: Towards Understanding Failure Modes of Human Pose Estimation in Space
result.comment: 4 pages + references, 4 figures. Published in the Proceedings of SPAICE 2026 and i-SAIRAS 2026
result.summary: Reliable monitoring of astronauts is essential for safety, situational awareness, and autonomous assistance in space missions. While modern computer vision enables accurate human detection and pose estimation on Earth, its robustness in space environments remains largely unquantified due to limited data availability. We present AstroPIE-53, a pilot dataset of 53 annotated astronaut videos collected from publicly available mission footage. To respect copyright restrictions, we release video identifiers, reconstruction scripts, and dense annotations rather than raw videos. The dataset includes bounding boxes, challenge classes, and human-annotated pose failure tags. We benchmark state-of-the-art person detection and pose estimation models under realistic zero-shot deployment conditions and perform the first systematic failure analysis for astronaut monitoring. Our results reveal substantial performance degradation caused by occlusions, unusual body orientations, low contrast, and microgravity motion patterns.

AI.brief_summary: 发布 AstroPIE-53 数据集（53 段航天员视频，含框、难度类别与人工标注的姿态失败标签），并在零样本条件下评测现有人体检测与姿态估计模型，系统分析遮挡、异常朝向、低对比度和微重力运动导致的失败。
